findings.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:137 — P1 anchor=100: `b.cache[key] = idx` now publishes only after an unlocked full build, so concurrent `getOrCreateIndex` calls for one key each create a private index and the last writer alone receives future watch updates, leaving earlier successful callers on stale detached state; the cache lookup appears to deduplicate, but it happens before construction and cannot close this race.

pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:216 — P1 anchor=100: `s.search.TotalDocs()` iterates the Bleve cache without a read lock after the new narrow publication lock permits an asynchronous watch-triggered `BuildIndex` to mutate that map, so startup observability is coupled to concurrent cache mutation and can destabilize the server under writes; waiting for the initial build group is insufficient because the watcher is launched before this call.

pkg/server/module_server_test.go:36 — P1, confidence 100: `if dbType == "postgres" { t.Skip("skipping - test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.") }` removes the sole storage-server startup integration assertion from the Postgres CI path, so a Postgres-only regression in the eager `NewResourceServer` initialization change will ship without any automated acceptance signal despite the stated local-only rebuttal because CI never executes that local configuration.

pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:137 — P1 anchor=100: `b.cache[key] = idx` publishes the last of two concurrently built snapshots after the removed full-build lock, so a write committed after the first snapshot but included and indexed by the second can be silently lost when the stale first build overwrites the cache; the apparent `GetIndex` deduplication cannot prevent it because both callers observe the cache before either publication.

pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:216 — P1 (75): `s.search.TotalDocs()` can concurrently iterate Bleve's unprotected `b.cache` while an event-triggered `BuildIndex` executes `b.cache[key] = idx` after its shortened lock scope, producing Go's fatal `concurrent map iteration and map write` and terminating startup; the strongest rebuttal is that the poller waits 100ms, but it is asynchronous and an event/build can overlap this new read under load or scheduling delay.

pkg/server/module_server_test.go:36 — P1, confidence 100: `if dbType == "postgres" { t.Skip("skipping - test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.") }` silently changes acceptance of the stated Unified Storage Performance Optimizations from working on the supported PostgreSQL CI path to allowing that path to be untested, and the strongest rebuttal—that this is an environment-specific pre-existing failure—fails because neither the task nor an explicitly accepted follow-up authorizes trading the regression signal for this optimization away.

pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258 — P1 (anchor 100): Calling `s.Init(ctx)` with the constructor-created `context.WithCancel(context.Background())` makes the startup `GetResourceStats`/watch database calls deadline-free, so a stalled backend leaves server construction hung indefinitely rather than returning a controlled startup failure.

pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:137 — P1 (anchor 100): Because `b.cacheMu.Lock()` now occurs only after the full `builder(idx)` scan and `b.cache[key] = idx`, simultaneous cache misses for one resource each rebuild the entire index (and race to create the same file-backed index), so concurrent searches can multiply database work and fail or time out even though the final cache entry is valid.

pkg/server/module_server_test.go:36 — P2, confidence 100 — `if dbType == "postgres" { t.Skip("skipping - test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.") }` removes PostgreSQL CI coverage for an instrumentation-server integration test, and even if the strongest rebuttal is a pre-existing Drone flake, it fails because this "Unified Storage Performance Optimizations" task neither traces the workaround to the stated intent nor supplies a follow-up that restores the coverage.

pkg/server/module_server_test.go:36 — [100][P2] The added `if dbType == "postgres" { t.Skip("skipping - test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.") }` removes CI coverage of the changed constructor-time resource-server initialization for PostgreSQL, so a PostgreSQL-only startup failure will pass even though MySQL may still exercise the generic path.

goldens.comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

This test appears to be related to server startup behavior. The diff also shows significant changes to server initialization in server.go (moving Init() call to NewResourceServer constructor). adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:137 — P1 anchor=100: `b.cache[key] = idx` publishes the last of two concurrently built snapshots after the removed full-build lock, so a write committed after the first snapshot but included and indexed by the second can be silently lost when the stale first build overwrites the cache; the apparent `GetIndex` deduplication cannot prevent it because both callers observe the cache before either publication.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the lock scope was narrowed from wrapping the entire BuildIndex function (lines 88-89 removed: `b.cacheMu.Lock()` and `defer b.cacheMu.Unlock()`) to only protecting the cache assignment (lines 137-139: `b.cacheMu.Lock()`, `b.cache[key] = idx`, `b.cacheMu.Unlock()`). This means two concurrent calls to BuildIndex for the same key can both proceed through the expensive index building process simultaneously. If the first build starts, then a write occurs, then the second build starts (capturing the new write), but the first build finishes and writes to cache after the second build writes to cache, the stale index from the first build will overwrite the fresher index. The finding correctly identifies this race condition where the last-to-finish build wins regardless of which has more recent data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:216 — P1 (75): `s.search.TotalDocs()` can concurrently iterate Bleve's unprotected `b.cache` while an event-triggered `BuildIndex` executes `b.cache[key] = idx` after its shortened lock scope, producing Go's fatal `concurrent map iteration and map write` and terminating startup; the strongest rebuttal is that the poller waits 100ms, but it is asynchronous and an event/build can overlap this new read under load or scheduling delay.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two relevant changes: (1) In bleve.go, the lock scope was shortened - `b.cacheMu.Lock()` was moved from the beginning of BuildIndex to just before `b.cache[key] = idx`, meaning the cache write happens with a brief lock. (2) In search.go line 216, a new log statement `s.log.Info("search index initialized", "duration_secs", end-start, "total_docs", s.search.TotalDocs())` was added. The finding claims TotalDocs() iterates over the cache while BuildIndex could be writing to it. Looking at the code flow: init() calls TotalDocs() after the index building loop completes, and the watcher is started AFTER init() completes (the diff shows the order was changed to initialize search index before starting the watcher). However, the concern is valid because BuildIndex can be called from multiple goroutines during the init phase itself (the code shows goroutines being spawned in the init loop), and the shortened lock scope in bleve.go means iteration in TotalDocs() could race with the final cache assignment. This is a plausible race condition introduced by the combination of changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258 — P1 (anchor 100): Calling `s.Init(ctx)` with the constructor-created `context.WithCancel(context.Background())` makes the startup `GetResourceStats`/watch database calls deadline-free, so a stalled backend leaves server construction hung indefinitely rather than returning a controlled startup failure.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `NewResourceServer` creates a context with `ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())` at line 255 (visible in the existing code structure), and then the new code at lines 255-260 calls `s.Init(ctx)` with this background context. Looking at the `Init` method, it calls `s.search.init(ctx)` which in turn calls `s.backend.GetResourceStats(ctx, ...)` (visible in the search.go changes where ctx is now properly propagated). Since the context is derived from `context.Background()` with no deadline/timeout, if the database backend stalls, the server construction will hang indefinitely. This is a real defect - the constructor should either use a context with a timeout or accept a context parameter.
